channel.title: The Grumpy Chef Blog
channel.description: Restaurant profit recovery frameworks, food cost control, and menu engineering from a German Master Chef with 20+ years of operator experience.

item.title: Restaurant Supplier Price Increases: Handle Them Without the Death Spiral
item.description: When a supplier line jumps, the reflex is to raise menu prices. That reflex kills covers. Here is how to find the margin inside the plate instead - re-costing, cross-utilization, and consolidating spend.

item.title: Should You Open a Second Restaurant Location? The Pre-Expansion Checklist for Independent Operators
item.description: The dangerous part of opening a second restaurant location is not the build - it is replicating whatever Location 1 quietly leaks, at 2x. Built from a $370K loss and one kitchen that survived.

item.title: Restaurant Prime Cost: What It Is, Why It Beats Food Cost, and How to Calculate It
item.description: Prime cost is COGS plus total labour - and it matters more than food cost percentage. Includes the formula, a verified season arc from Grumpy Schnitzel (53.4% in May, 39.2% at July peak), and the three calculation errors that make your number look better than it is.

item.title: Restaurant Portion Control: How to Lock Margin Into Every Plate
item.description: Food cost is decided at the prep table, not the register. How a portion spec on every dish locks margin into the plate before the first ticket prints - and why the rush makes it worse without one.

item.title: Menu Cross-Utilization: How One Ingredient Can Carry Your Whole Menu
item.description: Most independents buy to the shelf and strand ingredients on single dishes. Here is how the Grumpy Schnitzel pork loin - schnitzel, burger, and 12-hour stock from the same cut - held food cost at 33.7% while sales nearly doubled.

item.title: How to Reduce Restaurant Food Waste: A Trim and Off-Cut Protocol
item.description: A trim-and-off-cut protocol that assigns every kitchen scrap a pre-decided second life - the system used at the Grumpy Schnitzel to hold food cost at 33.7% blended while sales nearly doubled.

item.title: Right Steps, Wrong Order: Why Your SOPs Aren't Saving You Money
item.description: A new cook followed the recipe to the letter and still plated an overcooked patty on a cold bun. The problem wasn't the steps — it was the sequence. Here's where sequence drift quietly leaks your food cost.

item.title: Why Do Your Best Chefs Always Burn Out? The Single-Point-of-Failure Problem
item.description: Your best chef burns out because the restaurant runs through them. A 2015 line-partner walkout shows why it's not burnout — it's a single-point-of-failure problem.

item.title: Why Does My Restaurant Have High Staff Turnover? The Leadership Problem
item.description: Restaurant staff turnover costs $5,864 per employee. The fix isn't higher pay — it's written systems, structured onboarding, and leadership that earns respect instead of demanding it.

item.title: Why Do Restaurant Systems Fail? The Relapse Cycle Explained
item.description: Restaurant systems collapse because operators revert under pressure. Learn the 4-stage relapse cycle and the accountability framework that makes systems stick.

item.title: The 72-Hour Profit Discovery: How to Find Hidden Money in Your Restaurant This Week
item.description: Find hidden profit leaks in your restaurant within 72 hours. The signature diagnostic process that typically finds $15,000 to $50,000 in annual recovery.

item.title: Systems Over Hustle: Why Hustle Culture Creates Expensive Jobs, Not Businesses
item.description: After 22 years in hospitality and 140 straight days of 80-hour weeks, I realized I didn't have a business. I had an expensive job. Here's what changed.

item.title: How to Lower Food Cost Without Cutting Quality
item.description: Stop chasing food cost percentage. Start tracking contribution margin — the metric that shows real profit per plate. Menu engineering approach from a Master Chef.

item.title: What Is Menu Engineering and How Does It Increase Restaurant Profit?
item.description: Menu engineering classifies every item by profitability and popularity using the Stars/Plowhorses/Puzzles/Dogs matrix.

item.title: Why Is My Restaurant Busy but Not Profitable?
item.description: Full dining room, empty bank account. The problem isn't revenue — it's prime cost and hidden profit leaks.

item.title: How Do I Price My Restaurant Menu Correctly?
item.description: Food cost percentage is a trap. Contribution margin — the actual dollars left after food cost — is what pays your rent.

item.title: What Is a Restaurant Profit Leak and How Do I Find Mine?
item.description: A profit leak is money leaving your restaurant that doesn't show up on your P&L. Most operators have 5-8 active leaks across 9 categories.

item.title: How to Do a 72-Hour Restaurant Audit
item.description: Three days. Nine categories. Find your biggest profit leak before the weekend. The 72-Hour Profit Discovery framework.

item.title: What's the Difference Between Food Cost Percentage and Contribution Margin?
item.description: The industry obsesses over food cost percentage. But a 22% food cost item can make you less money than a 35% item. Here's the math.

item.title: How Do Independent Restaurants Compete with Chains on Profitability?
item.description: Chains have purchasing power. You have speed. Here's how to use the 60% Capacity Rule to compete on profitability.

item.title: What Should a Restaurant Owner Track Daily to Protect Profit Margins?
item.description: Monthly P&L statements show averages. Daily tracking shows leaks. The 5 leading indicators every operator needs.

item.title: How to Rebuild a Failing Restaurant in 21 Days
item.description: The 21-Day Restaurant Recovery Protocol. Three weeks. Three phases. The framework that rebuilt a restaurant from $370K in debt.
